propositions: The store-wide compaction sweep executes one git log --full-history walk per ticket while holding the global store write lock, stalling all writers for minutes.
Per-ticket position-commit map misses fall through to per-event wildcard walks with leading pathspecs that defeat pruning, making deployed cost worse than one walk per ticket.
The sweep never re-yields mid-run: it probes write_lock_is_busy once before starting but not between tickets, so arriving writers wait for the entire run.
The scoped staging _commit_backfill uses unscoped git add -A, allowing a concurrent writer's in-flight event files to be swept into the compaction commit.
The fix hoists the history walk out of the lock by building one position-keyed map per sweep before taking any lock, then queries it per ticket inside the locked fold.
The ledger parity and walk count must be verified together: a path-keyed map would miss every lookup and silently fall back to per-event walks with correct output and no error.
